title: United Bans AI Agents From Booking Flights For Customers

quotes.text: November 11, 2026
quotes.for: Publication date of the AirlineGeeks report.

quotes.text: In the first such move by a U.S. airline, United will ban third-party AI from parts of its digital platforms and adjust its policies to prevent access via travel agencies and aggregators.
quotes.for: First such move by a U.S. airline.

quotes.text: Sharing account credentials with personal, third-party AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles
quotes.for: Statement on unintended purchases, account changes and MileagePlus miles.

quotes.text: The carrier also said AI actions could violate FAA and Department of Transportation regulations. As an example, it cited the requirement that passengers confirm in person that their bags do not contain banned items, such as explosives.
quotes.for: FAA and DOT regulations and in-person check-in confirmation regarding explosives.

quotes.text: United said its stance is in line with companies in the banking and retail sectors.
quotes.for: Comparison with companies in banking and retail.

quotes.text: The airline said it will update its Digital Trust Center to clarify the new restrictions.
quotes.for: Planned update to United's Digital Trust Center.

title: United Airlines just made a big change to flight bookings. Here’s why Delta and American aren’t following suit

quotes.text: The Chicago-based carrier updated its contract of carriage on Wednesday, prohibiting the use of AI agents to “make, modify or service a ticket, and/or purchase any service or product.”
quotes.for: Contract of carriage update and quoted prohibition clause.

quotes.text: Just last month, Southwest Airlines announced a plugin partnership with ChatGPT to “offer a simpler, more direct path from inspiration and discovery to booking options” with the airline.
quotes.for: Southwest Airlines' ChatGPT plugin partnership announced the prior month.

quotes.text: Delta and American both indicated to Fast Company that some AI tools have booking privileges on their systems, though they continue to evaluate the landscape.
quotes.for: Delta and American allowing some AI tools booking privileges while evaluating.

quotes.text: We currently support certain interactions with AI assistants when they can be appropriately authenticated, while maintaining additional safeguards for sensitive transactions,
quotes.for: Delta spokesperson statement on authenticated AI assistant interactions.

quotes.text: even if passengers use AI tools, they’re ultimately responsible for overseeing any actions and authorizing any transactions taken by these assistants on their behalf.
quotes.for: Delta's statement on passenger responsibility for AI actions and transactions.

quotes.text: Representatives for Southwest, JetBlue, Alaska, and Frontier airlines didn’t immediately respond to Fast Company’s requests for comment.
quotes.for: No immediate response from Southwest, JetBlue, Alaska and Frontier.

quotes.text: Shares of United fell 1.8% on Wednesday, while the broader S&P 500 Index rose 1.3%.
quotes.for: United share price and S&P 500 moves on November 11, 2026.

title: United is restricting AI agents from booking flights

quotes.for: Publication date of the Engadget report.

quotes.text: The airline joins a growing number of businesses, including JPMorgan Chase and Amazon, which block agents from using their products to avoid the security and privacy issues associated with them.
quotes.for: Comparison with JPMorgan Chase and Amazon blocking AI agents.

quotes.text: United would like to avoid association with any agent-based embarrassments, for instance when Meta's Muse leaked a user's address online.
quotes.for: Example of Meta's Muse leaking a user's address online.

quotes.text: The Wall Street Journal reports that United CEO Scott Kirby has been open about the company's reluctance to jump into agentic commerce. "To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman," Kirby said at an event on Tuesday.
quotes.for: Scott Kirby's middleman remark reported by The Wall Street Journal.

quotes.text: Luckily for United and other companies blocking AI agents, agentic commerce might not be taking off with regular people.
quotes.for: Engadget's assessment of consumer uptake for agentic commerce.

quotes.text: During its recent third-quarter earnings call, Uber shared that it handled 320 million trips and deliveries during the week of Halloween; of those, AI agents were responsible for 500 Uber Eats orders and only four rides.
quotes.for: Uber third-quarter call figures on AI-agent orders and rides.
